title: Make a place for your project on GitHub
goal: Create a GitHub repository for your project and link your project to it

steps.say: Open github.com and sign in. You can make a free account there if you do not have one.
steps.find: the sign in button on github.com

steps.say: Press the plus icon in the top right corner of any GitHub page and choose New repository.
steps.find: the plus icon in the top right corner

steps.say: Type a short name for the project in the Repository name box. Use letters, numbers and dashes.
Choose who can see it. Private means only you (and people you invite); Public means anyone on the internet. If unsure, choose Private.
Press Create repository. GitHub then shows the next steps for your project.
In Terminal, inside your project folder, follow the steps GitHub shows for a project you already have. Companion then checks that your project is linked to GitHub.
steps.find: the steps GitHub shows on the new repository page

instead.say: If Terminal says this is not a git repository, follow GitHub's other set of steps, the one that starts a new repository on the command line.
instead.find: the other set of steps on the new repository page
